executiveSummary: GM0273 passes the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service numerical contract and has a coherent official 2025 base: Putten in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland, 24,953 residents, density 293, 22.1% aged 65-plus, thirteen neighbourhoods in two districts, one BAG woonplaats, fourteen BRT settlement labels, Putten station, 28 public-transport stop areas and five logical A28/N303/N797/N798 links. Neighbourhood population sums to 24,940, only thirteen below the municipality control, which is consistent with rounded source cells rather than missing people. Operational release is nevertheless correction-required. Putten combines the Veluwe forest/recreation interface, more than sixty recreation parks, local rain-groundwater-sewer and sprengen dependencies, and a Randmeren/Nuldernauw water pathway. The model instead emits 1.081510 m of generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel flood depth through T+72 without a selected local boundary condition, reuses exactly one top-five neighbourhood order across eight unrelated active hazards, and places a controlled wildfire source inside officially registered mixed forest/heath in BU02730109 while ranking that source neighbourhood ninth of thirteen and assigning only 13 of its 85 residents affected. Static public context identifies 125 water structures, utility/provider/planning records, roads, rail, antennas, education sites and an external acute-care dependency; none proves live continuity, passability, capacity or recovery. Exact T+72 clearing, persistence and 'operational' labels lack accountable local actions and verified milestones. Unknown, NoData, register no-match and planning/static values must never be rendered as zero hazard, safe, open, available or recovered.

identity.summary: Official 2025 identity, regional assignment, centre and generalized boundary agree.
notes: Manifest, generated context and official features identify GM0273 as Putten in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland.
The generated centre 5.5811254, 52.2420872 lies inside the official generalized 2025 multipolygon.
The boundary feature is valid for 2025 and administrative geometry is not an incident or exposure footprint.

geography.summary: The administrative footprint is coherent but cannot encode Putten's forest, groundwater, drainage or Randmeren mechanisms.
notes: Putten combines urban/recreation areas, extensive Veluwe forest/heath, sprengen/stream and groundwater systems, and the Nuldernauw/Randmeren edge.
Generalized boundaries and neighbourhood centres do not encode terrain, soils, sewers, surface-water catchments, defences, fuels, buildings, road intersections or incident geometry.
Direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation, Randmeren/polder effects, local pluvial flooding and drought/groundwater effects require separate selected mechanisms.

demography.summary: The official municipality control and rounded neighbourhood totals are internally plausible.
notes: The municipality control is 24,953 residents; neighbourhood rows total 24,940, a difference of -13 or -0.052% consistent with source rounding.
Municipality statistics report 5,523 people aged 65-plus, 22.1%, and 2,914 one-person households; summed rounded neighbourhood age-65-plus cells total 5,535.
Registered residents are not incident-time occupancy and exclude many recreation visitors; affected resident-equivalents must not be labelled as all people present.

regionalDetail.summary: Thirteen neighbourhoods provide useful context but have explicit gaps and no physical hazard calibration.
notes: All thirteen neighbourhoods carry the principal population/geography fields; cars-per-household is available in twelve, while district-heating percentage and public charging points are unavailable in all thirteen.
Largest resident rows are Putten-Zuid-Oost 6,220, Putten-Stationsstraat industriegebied 4,345, Putten-Zuid-West 3,340, Putten-Noord 2,730 and Verspreide huizen Norden, Bijsteren en Hoef 2,415.
Neighbourhood statistics, registered water assets, antennas, schools and provider/planning context do not establish exposure, continuity, backup, route access or restoration. Null remains Unknown.

settlements.summary: BAG and BRT settlement membership is coherent when their distinct semantics are preserved.
notes: BAG assigns one woonplaats, Putten; BRT supplies fourteen labels consisting of four woonkernen and ten buurtschappen.
BAG address-place registration and cartographic BRT labels are complementary and must not be treated as duplicate populations or complete occupancy zones.
Holiday parks, woodland visitors, workplaces, schools, station passengers and dispersed homes require incident-time exposure inputs rather than settlement-label inference.

transport.summary: Road, rail and transit identities are plausible, but event-valid access and external-care routing are unknown.
notes: The deployed logical graph has five A28/N303/N797/N798 links; Putten station and 28 stop areas are inside the municipality.
No scoped live NDW situation lies inside and no road/rail closure, direction, hazard intersection, forest/recreation access, accessible throughput or operator state is selected.
St Jansdal Harderwijk is external; straight-line proximity does not prove a usable route, referral, receiving capacity or continuity.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative risk, nature-fire, water and infrastructure context exists, but decision-ready local state and capacity do not.
notes: VNOG and Putten identify material nature-fire, flood, weather, heat/drought, utility, telecom/ICT and cyber concerns, including recreation populations and emergency access.
No selected incident supplies owner, issue/valid time, geometry/target, measured state, probability, uncertainty, response capacity or accountable first-72-hour decisions.
Zero assigned observation/care/service-point records, provider no-match and static/planning records retain NoData/context semantics.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six checkpoints across all eight services.
notes: Focused audit:model covers T+0, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours for severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound.
The app scenario factory is a thin clone of the canonical sim-core presets; a controlled local wildfire reproduction was also executed against the same model.
Execution coverage does not establish local calibration: outputs are deterministic exercise indices, not observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, allocations, ledgers, burden and layer-invariance contracts pass.
notes: Outputs are finite and non-negative; availability remains in [0,1], zero-event behavior is exact, and cumulative person-hours are monotone.
All service allocations use the thirteen neighbourhoods and reconcile to the municipal control; service-layer choice does not mutate hazard state.
Arithmetic correctness is necessary but does not validate local forcing, physical allocation, service topology, actions or recovery.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Unsupported generic river depth and a common cross-hazard ranking contradict Putten's known geography.
notes: The river preset reports severity 0.334773 and floodDepthM 1.081510 at both T+24 and T+72 without a selected Rhine/Meuse/IJssel branch or local Randmeren, defence, pump, breach or hydraulic event.
At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share exactly the same first five neighbourhoods: BU02730005, BU02730007, BU02730003, BU02730108 and BU02730004.
The controlled fire begins inside official mixed forest/heath in BU02730109, yet the source neighbourhood ranks ninth of thirteen and only 13 of its 85 residents are allocated affected.

serviceDependencies.summary: Water control, utilities, forest access, transport and external care remain static or synthetic rather than causal.
notes: The 125 HWH records do not form an authority-approved pump-weir-sewer-surface-water-groundwater-wastewater graph and do not influence the model.
Provider and capacity samples, antennas and education points cannot support exact service continuity, backup, switching, priority, damage or restoration percentages.
Roads affect mobility/supply only through synthetic links; forest/recreation access, rail state, drainage no-match and external St Jansdal routing/capacity cannot influence response.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers close, but locally selected events, dependency evidence and accountable actions are absent.
notes: No water level/forecast, defence/pump state, rain hyetograph, groundwater state, fire perimeter/risk phase, route/rail status, cyber target, utility incident or facility state is selected.

Response lacks owner, trigger, request, decision, resources, dependencies, execution, verification, uncertainty and rollback for warning, evacuation/shelter, fire access, water control, route closure, external care, utility support and re-entry.
Person-hours are numerically attributable to modelled service deficits, but those deficits are not attributable to locally evidenced incidents or actions.

recovery72h.summary: Exact hazard clearing, persistent flood plateaus and operational labels lack local recovery milestones.
notes: River T+72 still reports 1.081510 m, severity 0.334773, 7,883 affected and approximately 659,305 deprived person-hours; facilities availability falls from 0.637918 at T+24 to 0.490325 while most other services plateau.
Compound T+72 retains 0.350569 m flood depth, cyber disruption 0.051308, 12,635 affected and approximately 893,052 deprived person-hours after rain and wind become zero.

Pluvial and wildfire forcing/affected counts become exact zero by T+72 and several scenarios are labelled operational without verified drainage, fire, access, utility, care, support or re-entry milestones.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, population and administrative memberships are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM0273 Putten, Gelderland, VNOG, the generalized boundary and centre agree. Thirteen rounded neighbourhood populations total 24,940 versus the 24,953 municipality control, a -0.052% difference; one BAG place and fourteen BRT labels have distinct valid semantics.
findings.action: Retain edition, rounding, suppression and register semantics; never convert exact-looking controls or settlement labels into incident-time occupancy.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic numerical and coverage contract passes.
findings.evidence: Ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services execute deterministically with finite bounded values, population/demand/delivery reconciliation, causal ledgers, monotone cumulative burden and layer invariance.
findings.action: Keep GM0273 in regression and add local river-scope, hazard-specific allocation, forest-source containment, visitor exposure, NoData and recovery-action assertions.

findings.summary: The river preset emits unsupported direct named-major-river inundation for Putten.
findings.evidence: At T+24 and T+72 floodDepthM is 1.081510 and severity 0.334773; affected resident-equivalents rise from 7,156 to 7,883 and burden reaches about 659,305 person-hours. No Rhine/Meuse/IJssel branch, Nuldernauw/Randmeren boundary, Putten-area defence/pump state, breach, hydraulic grid, arrival, recession or uncertainty is selected.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing generic major-river depth, exposure and recovery. Add separately named, authority-selected Randmeren/polder and indirect supply events; unselected local cells remain Unknown, not dry or safe.

findings.summary: Zero direct open-coast depth is a narrow model statement, not a Putten water-safety conclusion.
findings.evidence: The coastal preset reports zero local flood depth and affected residents, while retaining low wind/service burden. Putten is not open coast, but Nuldernauw/Randmeren, local surface water, groundwater, drainage and indirect access/supply pathways are separate mechanisms not tested by that zero.
findings.action: Label open-coast direct impact separately and never generalize it to Randmeren, polder, pluvial, groundwater, wind, access or supply safety.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse exactly one top-five neighbourhood allocation order.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank BU02730005, BU02730007, BU02730003, BU02730108 and BU02730004 first in the same order. The allocation seed is independent of mechanism and source location, so it cannot represent hydraulics, heat/vulnerability, vegetation/smoke, wind exposure or cyber targets.
findings.action: Replace the shared rank with hazard-specific physical/target surfaces and reject full cross-hazard rank reuse in tests; unsupported neighbourhood cells stay Unknown.

findings.summary: A controlled wildfire fails source-neighbourhood containment in official mixed forest/heath.
findings.evidence: At the BU02730109 forest-neighbourhood centre inside ISOR Putten193 and BRT gemengd bos, T+24 severity is 0.425986, flame 0.401521, smoke 0.449104 and 3,771 residents are affected. Yet BU02730109 ranks ninth of thirteen and receives only 13 affected of 85 residents while the generic top five are unchanged.
findings.action: Require eligible current vegetation, ignition/perimeter, weather, spread/smoke, buildings/people including visitors, emergency access/water and incident-command evidence; assert source-cell containment before releasing local exposure.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure omits Putten's material recreation population and place-time demand.
findings.evidence: Putten reports more than sixty recreation parks and designated clusters at Koudhoorn, Krachtighuizen and Huinen, with visitor gateways at Putterbos, Krachtighuizerheide and Schovenhorst. Tourist-tax records distinguish visitors from registered residents, but affected counts are capped and allocated only against the 24,953 resident control.
findings.action: Add privacy-safe, time-banded visitor/work/school/station/recreation cohorts with authoritative provenance and uncertainty; keep resident-equivalents and estimated persons present visibly separate.

findings.summary: Precise pluvial depth and clearance omit Putten's evolving sewer-groundwater-surface-water evidence.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports 0.336048 m, severity 0.242701, 1,470 affected and about 85,321 person-hours, then depth and affected count are zero at T+72. Municipal evidence says SSW/isohypse work improved insight while regional groundwater monitoring and further water-nuisance/heat studies were being developed; no selected rain, DEM, initial groundwater/surface-water, sewer/pump state or intervention edition drives the values.
findings.action: Use the governing stress-test/rain, terrain, groundwater, sewer and surface-water evidence with issue/valid time, resolution, assumptions and NoData; separate pluvial flooding, groundwater nuisance, sprengen drought and water-quality pathways.

findings.summary: Forest access, A28/N-road/rail continuity and external acute-care transfer are not event-valid dependencies.
findings.evidence: Five logical road links, Putten station and 28 stop areas are static context; no scoped NDW situation or rail operating state is selected. Putten stresses emergency-service access in nature areas, while no RIVM acute-care site is inside and St Jansdal Harderwijk is about 11.4 km straight-line away. None can influence response through closure, hazard intersection, direction, referral or destination state.
findings.action: Add event-valid, direction-aware routes to forest/recreation sites, shelters/support points, utilities and external care using operator/authority status; never infer travel, capacity or passability from distance, maps or schedules.

findings.summary: Public water, utility, antenna and education records do not justify exact service trajectories.
findings.evidence: HWH assigns 125 realized structures but no approved connected operating graph; one electricity sample is planning context; provider point results, 60 installations/123 antennas and 20 education locations do not expose live state, backup, switching, occupancy or restoration. Drainage provider no-match and zero local monitoring/service-point records are NoData, but every service receives exact availability/recovery values.
findings.action: Use operator/authority-approved safe aggregate incident and restoration bands with explicit provenance; expose coverage and Unknown, and add first-72-hour support/communications actions without inventing sensitive topology.

findings.summary: Wind, heat, winter, cyber and remote-earthquake outputs are synthetic and not locally calibrated.
findings.evidence: No selected local weather observation, heat/vulnerability surface, winter road state, cyber target/incident or earthquake event is bound. The canonical Groningen earthquake yields zero local ground motion, severity and affected count for Putten but still accumulates about 13,555 to 23,466 person-hours through synthetic indirect network effects.
findings.action: Keep outputs labelled as exercise assumptions and direct-versus-indirect effects; require source, target/geometry, issue/valid time, units, uncertainty, coverage, licence and NoData before operational interpretation.

findings.summary: T+72 plateaus, exact clearing and operational status lack owner-verified recovery milestones.
findings.evidence: River depth persists at 1.081510 while facilities worsen and most services plateau; compound depth persists at 0.350569 with 12,635 affected and about 893,052 person-hours; pluvial and wildfire forcing/affected counts become exact zero. No pump/drainage, fire all-clear, route/rail, utility, care, support or re-entry action verifies those transitions.
findings.action: Replace exact recovery claims with uncertainty envelopes and an owner-trigger-decision-resource-execution-verification ledger; keep state Unknown until accountable milestones are met.

corrections.summary: Suppress generic GM0273 named-major-river output and add a distinct authority-selected Randmeren/local-water event contract.
corrections.validation: Require a named authority-selected event with Randmeren/local boundary condition, datum, defence/pump/breach/overtopping state, protected side, connected depth/velocity/arrival/recession evidence, issue/valid time, probability/uncertainty, resolution, coverage, NoData and licence. Direct exposure/recovery remains Unknown until selected; tests reject the present generic 1.081510 m output.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared GM0273 spatial seed with source-aware physical hazard allocation and dynamic recreation exposure.
corrections.validation: Use hydraulic/rain-flow cells for water, shade/building/vulnerability for heat, eligible vegetation/perimeter/plume for fire/smoke, wind exposure and asset targets for cyber. A controlled ignition inside BU02730109 must include/rank the source cell under documented assumptions; unrelated hazards may not reuse the full order. Show residents separately from privacy-safe time-banded visitors/work/school/transit exposure.

corrections.summary: Integrate versioned Putten sewer-groundwater-surface-water evidence and a safe aggregate water/utility dependency graph.
corrections.validation: Reconcile municipality, water-board, HWH and operator evidence only into approved non-sensitive compartments with compatible units, current state, power/backup and uncertainty. Bind rain/terrain/groundwater/sewer/surface-water editions and distinguish drought/sprengen. Planning, register status, no-match and zero assigned observation points cannot generate operational, dry or recovered state.

corrections.summary: Add event-valid forest/recreation, A28/N-road/rail and external-care access dependencies.
corrections.validation: Use road/traffic, rail/operator, municipality/fire-region and GHOR/RIVM authority state. Intersect selected hazards with direction-aware access to nature/recreation sites, neighbouring corridors, station/rail, support points and St Jansdal/other selected destinations. Record issue/valid time, accessibility and Unknown capacity; static maps, schedules and distance never prove passage or care acceptance.

corrections.summary: Replace exact GM0273 first-72-hour recovery labels with accountable actions, milestones and uncertainty.
corrections.validation: For warning, evacuation/shelter, water control, fire response/all-clear, road/rail access, utilities, external care, vulnerable-person/visitor support and re-entry, store owner, trigger, request, decision, resources, dependencies, execution, verification, uncertainty and rollback. Tests reject exact clearance, plateaus and operational/recovered labels without verified milestones.

residualLimitations: This audit assesses a deterministic exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic/fire assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, route guarantee, clinical referral or operator commitment.
CBS 2025 neighbourhood values are rounded/suppressed; the -13 population difference and age-band sum difference are not evidence of missing or extra incident-time people.
Registered residents exclude incident-time recreation visitors, workers, pupils, station passengers and people in nature areas; public pages do not supply a complete time-varying occupancy series.
Generalized municipal/neighbourhood boundaries and centre points are unsuitable for terrain, sewer, drainage, defence, vegetation, building, asset, smoke or route-intersection calculations.
Nuldernauw/Randmeren identity and regional flood risk do not establish a current local water level, defence/pump state, breach, hydraulic footprint, probability or arrival/recession.
No complete governing Putten rain hyetograph/raster, DEM/intervention edition, initial groundwater/surface-water state, sewer model or stress-test output is consumed.
Municipal SSW, isohypse, monitoring and DAPPER programme evidence describes knowledge and work, not a live incident or completed operational measure.

ISOR/BRT forest intersections support land-cover eligibility only; old record metadata and static classification do not establish current fuel, moisture, ignition, perimeter, spread, smoke or response state.
HWH's 125 assigned records have partial coverage and source-specific capacity properties; realized/register presence is not connectivity, compatible throughput, live operation, backup or restoration.
The water board's 2026-09-02 drought picture is a regional time-stamped snapshot, not a substitute for scenario-time local measurements or arbitrary T+0–72 states.
NWB, GTFS and ProRail context does not establish live road/rail direction, passability, accessibility, emergency throughput, station operation or destination access.
No RIVM acute-care location lies inside GM0273; St Jansdal registration and straight-line distance do not establish referral, route, occupancy, staffing, diversion, generator endurance or acceptance.
One NBNL postcode sample and point provider results are planning/responsibility context, not complete municipal topology, current load, incident, switching, priority, reserve or restoration.
RDI and DUO records identify registered antennas and education-use locations, not telecom coverage/backhaul/power or occupancy/shelter/staffing/continuity.
Zero assigned Waterinfo, KNMI, PM2.5, NDW and government-service-point records and drainage-provider no-match are scoped coverage gaps, not zero hazard, safety, open access or absent service.
No selected local weather, fire, flood, cyber, utility, transport or care incident is bound by publisher, issue/valid time, geometry/target, units, uncertainty, coverage and licence.
Exact synthetic availability can be numerically reconciled without validating physical causality, capacity, response decisions or recovery.
Recovery beyond T+72, warning lead, mutual aid, shelter/support capacity, health effects, animal/livestock needs and long-term re-entry remain outside locally validated scope.
